source.facts: Confirmed by Winston (Nov 2026): 1st place, UW Blueprint Designathon 2025; one-day event; team of four (Ishan, Raghav, Lily, Winston); brainstormed together, picked the idea after brainstorming, then split screens; Winston worked on bits of everything and it was a group effort, so the case study should not say who did what; submitted a clickable prototype and a pitch deck; no specific judge feedback; the move from automatic matching to student-hosted sessions was not a deliberate decision; map-first home because location matters and it is visually engaging; the polished screens ('Final WINSTON') were made by Winston after the event. Prompt: 'How might we design solutions that help people connect, care, and thrive empowering the individual and the community?'

fields.description: A campus study app concept that won 1st place at the UW Blueprint Designathon 2025.
fields.intro: CoStudy is an app concept for finding and joining study sessions for your courses on campus. My team of four designed it in one day and won 1st place at the UW Blueprint Designathon 2025.
fields.summary: “How might we design solutions that help people connect, care, and thrive, empowering the individual and the community?”
fields.overview: The designathon gave us the prompt above. We brainstormed ideas as a team, picked one, then split up the screens. It was a group effort, and I worked on a bit of everything. We submitted a clickable prototype and a pitch deck.

sections.title: Idea
sections.heading: From prompt to a study app
content: We started from the prompt and brainstormed about 16 ideas, from micro-volunteering to a neighbourhood emergency app. Then we picked one together: an automatic study-group generator that would put students into groups and assign a spot on campus. The prototype ended up with students hosting their own sessions instead.

content.alt: Part of the team’s idea board: the designathon prompt surrounded by short ideas, with the automatic group study session generator below
content.caption: Part of our idea board. The study-group idea is at the bottom.

sections.title: Home
sections.heading: A map of who’s studying where
content: Home puts a campus map first, with your sessions in a sheet below. We put the map first for two reasons:

bullets: **Location matters:** where a session is decides whether you can go.

content: On the day, we agreed in Figma comments to keep gradients for live sessions and your upcoming ones only.

content.alt: Two iPhones: the CoStudy home with a campus map and stacked course icons above a sheet of your sessions, and the sheet pulled up with tinted live sessions above plain upcoming ones
content.caption: The map, and the sheet pulled up.

sections.title: Joining
sections.heading: What changes when you join
content: Joining is one tap. After that, the main button becomes “Open class thread” and a Leave session button appears. On the day, we also agreed to add a list of people attending.

content.alt: Two iPhones: a CoStudy session before joining with a Join session button, and after joining with Open class thread and Leave session
content.caption: Before and after joining.

sections.title: Sign-up
sections.heading: Courses come pre-filled
content: Sign-up verifies a school email, then shows your courses pre-filled for you to confirm. Each course gets a colour that follows it through the app.

content.alt: Three iPhones: the CoStudy welcome screen, the university email step, and course confirmation with four pre-filled courses in their colours
content.caption: Welcome, school email and course confirmation.

sections.title: After the event
sections.heading: Polishing it afterwards
content: After the designathon, I polished the main screens on my own, including a more detailed campus map, a blue accent and a lighter Threads header.

content.alt: Two iPhones: the CoStudy home as submitted at the designathon, and the home polished afterwards with a more detailed campus map and a blue button
content.caption: As submitted, and polished after the event.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.heading: Result and what’s still assumed
content: We won 1st place, but we didn’t get any specific feedback beyond the result.

bullets: There are enough sessions to fill the map.
Students are comfortable showing where they study.
The app can get a student’s courses from the school.
